properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 is the extension's core account-signing curve (Ethereum ECDSA + BIP-32 key derivation): capability ships via declared dependencies (secp256k1@4.0.4 resolutions, elliptic, @noble/curves/secp256k1 — direct import only in the seedless e2e helper), is granted in every lavamoat build policy, is documented in Snap permission descriptions across the locale files (snap_getBip32Entropy/PublicKey for secp256k1 — those locale sites are prose, not call sites), and the production ECIES QR-sync key

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Hardcoded credential material, by design: Transak/MoonPay/CoinbasePay publishable (client-embeddable) API keys in app/scripts/constants/on-ramp.ts:1-3 ship in the bundle — MoonPay's is a live publishable key ('pk_live_'). The remaining sites are ERC-20 contract addresses and mock OIDC tokens in test fixtures — non-secret values the rule matched. Kept as the on-ramp credential inventory; publishable keys are not protectable secrets but are key-like material embedded client-side.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: EVP_BytesToKey (legacy OpenSSL MD5-based KDF) capability ships in the bundle via the crypto-browserify shim: every lavamoat build policy (mv2/mv3, beta/experimental/flask/main) grants crypto-browserify>browserify-cipher>evp_bytestokey. No first-party call site (grep confirms only policy grants and attribution.txt); used by browserified dependencies if invoked. Legacy KDF, retained as shipped-capability inventory.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Math.random used across the app for non-security randomness: RPC request/action IDs, telemetry and lazy-load sampling, Shield marketing-cohort selection, UI notification IDs, test fixtures and address fixtures. One security-relevant case: shared/lib/delegation/delegation.ts:180 derives the EIP-7702 delegation 'salt' from Math.random (~32 bits, weak PRNG) — should use crypto.getRandomValues; also generate-metametrics-id.ts hashes Math.random entropy for the analytics client ID. Cryptographic rand

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: RSA-2048 keypair generated at runtime by an e2e test helper to populate manifest flags for testing. Quantum-vulnerable primitive but ephemeral, test-only keygen; not shipped in the extension build.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: secp256k1 declared as a dependency in package.json — the Ethereum signing curve (ECDSA over secp256k1) used by the extension's keyrings. Shor-vulnerable; core migration item for account signatures.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: UTC/V3 JSON keystore test fixture using aes-128-ctr + KDF — the keystore format the extension's account-import flow decrypts. AES-128-CTR is unauthenticated and quantum-relevant only via Grover; the fixture documents a format the app must support, test file only.

components.name: Node.js tls sessions on default settings (at least Node.js 24.13.0)

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Outbound HTTPS session to sourcify.dev (contract metadata lookup) opened with a plain fetch() and no TLS configuration — host-default key exchange. In the extension runtime this is Chromium's TLS stack (offers hybrid X25519MLKEM768 by default on current builds); under Node dev/test it is Node 24.13 defaults (OpenSSL 3.5.x, ML-KEM hybrid available). No pinning, no custom cipher/group list; posture depends on the runtime, changeable only by the platform.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Ed25519 capability: production rewards code declares signatureType 'ed25519' (Solana Snap signature verification, app/scripts/controllers/rewards/utils/solana-snap.ts:9), lavamoat policies grant ed25519 and ed25519Bip32 Snap curve capabilities (BIP-32 entropy for Ed25519 curves), tweetnacl (NaCl Ed25519) is a declared dependency used in solana-wallet-standard e2e helpers, and @noble/curves provides it. Shor-vulnerable signature scheme; migration ML-DSA-65 when Solana/PQ standards land.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDH capability ships in the bundled build: lavamoat policies grant crypto-browserify>create-ecdh (the Node ECDH shim) for browserified dependencies; no first-party ECDH call site found — the qr-sync pairing uses ECIES via eciesjs (reported as a separate finding) and the seedless fixtures show secp256k1-ephemeral ECIES blobs. Quantum-vulnerable key agreement capability present in the shipped bundle.

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: ECDSA capability in the rewards feature: Bitcoin Snap attestations carry signatureType 'ecdsa' (production rewards controllers plus their tests), granted via lavamoat policies, and ECDSA-256 fixtures in the seedless e2e helpers (the same mock P-256 key). The extension's primary ECDSA use is secp256k1 Ethereum signing inside keyring libraries (covered by the secp256k1 object). Shor-vulnerable; migration ML-DSA-65.

properties.name: pqs:context

properties.name: pqs:context
properties.value: Deep-link signature verification — a documented SECURITY BOUNDARY: shared/lib/deep-links/verify.ts uses WebCrypto ECDSA over P-256 with SHA-256 (importKey namedCurve 'P-256' at :42-48, subtle.verify at :79 and :107) to verify signed deep links against a pinned public key (production key injected via DEEP_LINK_PUBLIC_KEY env; test key via manifest flags). Shor-vulnerable authentication of deep links; migration to ML-DSA-based signatures when the WebAuthn/JWS PQ ecosystem lands. Test mirror at tes
